name: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)
description: The world's largest government-funded health assurance scheme covers over 10 crore poor and vulnerable families for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization.
target_group: Poor and vulnerable families are identified based on SECC 2011 data and existing RSBY beneficiaries.
benefits: It provides a health cover of up to INR 5 lakhs per family per year for cashless hospitalization, covering over 1,949 medical packages.
how_to_apply: Beneficiaries are automatically identified, and eligibility can be checked online or by calling the national helpline 14555/1800-111-565.

name: Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness Centres (AB-HWCs)
description: This initiative transforms existing health centres into AB-HWCs to provide comprehensive primary health care (CPHC) closer to the community.
target_group: The target group is the entire population, focusing on delivering primary healthcare services to rural and urban communities.
benefits: It offers free universal access to CPHC services, including NCD care and free essential medicines and diagnostics.
how_to_apply: Services are provided directly at the local AB-HWC; no formal application process is required for primary care services.

name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP)
description: This campaign provides quality generic medicines at affordable prices to the masses through dedicated Jan Aushadhi Kendras.
target_group: The target group is all citizens seeking affordable and quality generic medicines.
benefits: It provides access to over 1,800 generic medicines and surgical instruments at significantly lower prices (50-90% less) than branded options.
how_to_apply: Medicines can be purchased directly from any Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendra by presenting a valid prescription.

name: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK)
description: This initiative eliminates out-of-pocket expenses for pregnant women and sick newborns accessing public health institutions to ensure safe motherhood and child survival.
target_group: The target group includes all pregnant women delivering in public health institutions and sick newborns up to one year of age.
benefits: It provides free delivery (including C-section), essential drugs, diagnostics, blood, diet, and transport services.
how_to_apply: Benefits are automatically provided to eligible beneficiaries at public health facilities; no separate application is required.

name: Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK)
description: This is a child health screening and early intervention service program for children from birth to 18 years of age under the National Health Mission (NHM).
target_group: The target group is children from birth to 18 years, including newborns, infants, pre-school, and school-going children.
benefits: It provides comprehensive screening for 4 D's (Defects, Deficiencies, Diseases, and Developmental delays), with free treatment and referrals.
how_to_apply: Screening is conducted by Mobile Health Teams at anganwadis and schools, and parents can also approach public health facilities.

name: National Health Mission (NHM)
description: This umbrella program aims to achieve universal access to equitable, affordable, and quality healthcare services.
target_group: The target group is the entire population, focusing on rural and urban poor, vulnerable sections, women, and children.
benefits: It strengthens public health infrastructure, improves access to MCH services, controls diseases, and provides free essential drugs and diagnostics.
how_to_apply: Benefits are accessed via public health facilities (Sub-Centres, PHCs, CHCs, District Hospitals) and community health workers (ASHA).

name: National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP)
description: A national program aimed at eliminating Tuberculosis from India by 2025 by providing free diagnosis and treatment services to all affected individuals.
target_group: The target group is all individuals suspected of or diagnosed with Tuberculosis (TB).
benefits: It offers free diagnosis, free anti-TB drugs, nutritional support (Nikshay Poshan Yojana) of INR 500 per month, and follow-up care.
how_to_apply: Individuals with TB symptoms should visit the nearest government health facility or designated microscopy centre for free testing and treatment.

name: National AIDS Control Programme (NACP)
description: A comprehensive program to prevent new HIV infections and provide care, support, and treatment to people living with HIV (PLHIV).
target_group: The target group includes the general population for prevention, high-risk groups (HRGs), pregnant women, and people living with HIV (PLHIV).
benefits: It provides free HIV testing and counselling, free Anti-Retroviral Treatment (ART), prevention of parent-to-child transmission (PPTCT) services, and extensive awareness campaigns.
how_to_apply: Services are available at Integrated Counselling and Testing Centres (ICTCs), ART Centres, and designated health facilities nationwide.

name: Employees' State Insurance Scheme (ESIS)
description: A social security and health insurance scheme providing comprehensive medical care and cash benefits to organized sector workers.
target_group: Employees in establishments with 10 or more persons earning up to INR 21,000 per month (or INR 25,000 for persons with disability).
benefits: It includes comprehensive medical care for the insured person and family, sickness benefit, maternity benefit, and disablement benefit.
how_to_apply: Employers are responsible for registering eligible employees with ESIC; beneficiaries receive an ESI card to avail services.

name: Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS)
description: A healthcare scheme providing comprehensive medical care facilities to central government employees, pensioners, and certain other categories.
target_group: Central Government employees (serving and retired), MPs, Judges, Journalists, and their dependents in CGHS covered cities.
benefits: It offers outpatient and inpatient care, specialist consultation, supply of medicines, and investigations through CGHS facilities and empaneled hospitals.
how_to_apply: Eligible individuals apply for a CGHS card through their respective departments or the CGHS portal to access services.
